title: The Road Not Taken: A Reflection on Life’s Choices

content.body: The Road Not Taken by Robert Frost is one of the most memorable poems in literature. However, on this blog, I do not care about how famous a poem was or became; I care about the message it delivers, be it big or small, and I try to relate to it. After reading this poem and then trying to understand its meaning, I have gained or at least been reminded of a healthy perspective to view life. If you are a dreamer, not happy with small things, or if you believe that you work hard but do not get the results, then this poem presents a good reflection and reminder for you.

Frost finds himself at a fork in the road on an autumn day and cannot decide which path to take. The purpose of his journey is not mentioned. Maybe he is just on a walk to see things around. Neither is there any signage to guide him. Due to time constraints, he can only take one of these paths. Also, sadly, he cannot make out which path is more valuable because the dense forest makes both of them equally mysterious. Thus, having concluded that the future cannot be determined, Frost begins to make irrational reasons that do not help him at all. For example, one path is inviting ‘more wear.’ While we, the readers, view this situation as non-trivial, Frost feels FOMO. Maybe there is some treasure on the path that he does not take. At last, he takes the path less traveled and concludes that decision made all the difference in the world for him.

content.subheading: The Metaphor: How Beautifully it is Painted Here
content.body: In my interpretation, this non-trivial situation of choosing paths is a metaphor for life’s small and big decisions. If you take this poem literally, then you might view the described event as something non-trivial. However, only those who are told about this metaphor will understand what the poet is trying to convey. Notice how the picture in the poem is painted as simply as the fork on the road. There is no context given in terms of the purpose of the journey. There is no guiding signboard as well. Life to me is exactly the same. We make decisions every day: small and big. And we do this while we have no clue of what will become of us. Yes, we do set goals and make friends or find mentors who help us, but from an absurdist point of view, these are just illusions that we like to believe in.

It would be convenient if the poet could come back and try the other path. However, Frost apologizes that it cannot happen. This is not because he does not have time, but to convey that we cannot go back and change our decisions. It’s a hard truth. So it’s wise to spend every moment invested in life’s beauty. Thus, it’s a huge call to action for us to get out of Instagram and work hard. Because there won’t be a second chance.

content.subheading: How Much Can We Make Choices About the Future?
content.body: There is a moment in which Frost tries to peek into the paths. It’s a reasonable strategy to look into the future and try to find out what will become of us. However, there are only a few steps before the path turns and is eaten into that dense ‘undergrowth.’ This depicts the uncertainty of life. At some moments of life, we cannot know anything about the future. Investing in resources to know more about the future might be a futile and counter-productive effort. I think it’s good to realize this as early as possible so that even if you fail, you can at least be assured that you didn’t waste much time in thinking to make a bad decision.

content.subheading: Power of Choice in Youth. Regret in Old Age.
content.body: While we are talking about how important every moment is, we should note that perspective matters. Frost demonstrates the difference in perspective through the eyes of the same poet during different times of life. The present narrator that has this problem in front of him decides to take a random path today and then come back again another day to try out the other path. Therefore, the poet purchases to blindly follow a path with the resource of time he has. There is a saying that there is always a tomorrow. And the present narrator celebrates this lavishness. However, we are also provided the perspective of a future narrator that reflects on the happening of these decisions. This perspective has wisdom and knows that maybe the poet could have come back, but it would have been different. This perspective states that the decision his former self made on that day in particular autumn had weight and consequence in changing the events of his life.

As a 22-year-old, I am thankful for this reminder. I have a bad habit of procrastinating, and my comfort is that I have a lot of time. Especially now that I am out of college, I know I can take things slowly at my own time. But now I do realize how sad my future self would be when I look back. I think this is a needed message— Time is running out. Maybe I will get a picture of an hourglass and put it on my wall.

This poem is especially famous for the poet’s undertaking of a journey that is ‘less traveled,’ meaning that it was harder. However, to me, it does not suffice to always take a journey less traveled. Yes, we should be courageous in all endeavors, but to choose a path simply because it’s less traveled is not logical. However, I agree that you should not conform.

In conclusion, as a young adult, I have many dreams and interests. This gives me happiness in the moment because I can possibly become so many things. I am not restricted. I have the power of choice. But this too shall one day be taken away. And I will always regret it. Life is beautiful now as I have a choice. In ‘Man’s Search For Meaning,’ Viktor Frankl inspiringly tells:

“There were always choices to make. Every day, every hour, offered the opportunity to make a decision, a decision which determined whether you would or would not submit to those powers which threatened to rob you of your very self, your inner freedom; which determined whether or not you become the plaything to circumstance, renouncing freedom and dignity.”

We always forget this. Maybe after writing this blog post, I will also go back to my previous self—uninspired by the beauty of life. To not let this happen, I will have to exercise being more in the present. I mean, that is how the poet was inspired to write this wonderful poem. What seemed to us as a little navigation problem became an existential crisis for him because he decided to stop and actually observe the problem. He did not just pass by the moment. He took joy in living in it.

So from now on, when someone asks me what my hobbies or interests are, I am always going to say to appreciate the moment.
